milestones.label: Linear-programming upper bounds
milestones.work: H. Cohn and N. Elkies, New upper bounds on sphere packings I, Ann. Math. 157 (2003)
milestones.description: The upper-bound method preceded the exact optimality proofs.

evidence.claim: Annals record dates the bounds paper to 2003.

milestones.label: Dimension-eight optimality proved
milestones.work: M. Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 8, arXiv:1603.04246 (2016)
milestones.description: Viazovska proved the E8 lattice packing optimal in eight dimensions.

evidence.claim: Public preprint dated March 2016 states the optimality theorem.

milestones.label: Dimension-twenty-four optimality proved
milestones.work: H. Cohn et al., The sphere packing problem in dimension 24, arXiv:1603.06518 (2016)
milestones.description: A second public paper proved the Leech lattice optimal in twenty-four dimensions.

evidence.claim: Public preprint dated March 2016 states the 24-dimensional result.

works.citation: The sphere packing problem in dimension 8
The sphere packing problem in dimension 24

notes: The two dimensions are separate phases in March 2016. A first successful application of the exact auxiliary-function method beyond these examples and institutional naming remain open.

canonicalName: Random partitions, representation theory and Gromov-Witten theory

milestones.label: Infinite wedge applied to random partitions
milestones.work: A. Okounkov, Infinite wedge and random partitions, arXiv:math/9907127 (1999)
milestones.description: The public preprint uses integrable-systems techniques to obtain exact random-partition correlations.

evidence.claim: The 1999 abstract states the correlation-function results.

milestones.label: Completed cycles link Hurwitz and Gromov–Witten theory
milestones.work: A. Okounkov and R. Pandharipande, Gromov–Witten theory, Hurwitz theory, and completed cycles, Ann. Math. 163 (2006)
milestones.description: The paper connects Hurwitz counting with Gromov–Witten invariants through completed cycles.

evidence.claim: Annals record identifies the 2006 paper and its subject.

notes: The event bundles several domains. The earliest public statement of the whole bridge and the exact first use in a target Gromov–Witten problem need comparison with earlier Okounkov–Pandharipande preprints; the 2006 paper is a documented development, not an unqualified first application.

canonicalName: Measure rigidity and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity

milestones.label: Measure rigidity proves arithmetic QUE
milestones.work: E. Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity, Ann. Math. 163 (2006)
milestones.description: A positive-entropy measure classification yields arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity for compact arithmetic surfaces.

evidence.claim: The Annals abstract states the measure classification and arithmetic QUE consequence.

works.citation: Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity
works.whyItMatters: Established arithmetic QUE through measure classification

notes: The Annals landing-page heading omits “quantum,” while the original paper and DOI metadata contain it. The publisher lists receipt in March 2003, which is not a public publication date. An earlier public preprint may exist; until identified, conceptual and methodological first dates stay open.

canonicalName: Higher composition laws and arithmetic statistics

milestones.label: First higher composition-law paper published
milestones.work: M. Bhargava, Higher composition laws I: A new view on Gauss composition, and quadratic generalizations, Ann. Math. 159 (2004)
milestones.description: The paper generalizes Gauss composition using higher-dimensional parameterizations.

evidence.claim: Annals bibliographic record identifies the 2004 paper.

milestones.label: Composition framework applied to elliptic-curve statistics
milestones.work: M. Bhargava and A. Shankar, Binary quartic forms having bounded invariants, and the boundedness of the average rank of elliptic curves, Ann. Math. 181 (2015)
milestones.description: The paper counts quartic forms in a study of average ranks of elliptic curves.

evidence.claim: Annals record identifies the 2015 arithmetic-statistics paper.

milestones.note: This is a documented application, not established as the first use of higher composition laws in arithmetic statistics.

works.citation: Higher composition laws I: A new view on Gauss composition, and quadratic generalizations

notes: A 2001 thesis may predate the 2004 journal publication; its public availability must be checked. The 2015 target application is documented but may have predecessors; methodological priority remains open.

milestones.label: Unique Games Conjecture posed
milestones.work: S. Khot, On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games, STOC (2002)
milestones.description: Khot’s public conference paper formulates the hardness conjecture for unique two-prover games.

evidence.claim: ACM bibliographic record dates the conference paper to 2002.

works.citation: On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games

notes: Later approximation-hardness applications and the first institutional or textbook anchor remain to be researched.

milestones.label: Geometric complexity theory programme proposed
milestones.work: K. Mulmuley and M. Sohoni, Geometric Complexity Theory I: An Approach to the P vs. NP and Related Problems, SIAM J. Comput. 31 (2001)
milestones.description: The paper proposes a representation-theoretic geometry programme for P versus NP and related complexity questions.

evidence.claim: SIAM record identifies the named 2001 programme paper.

milestones.label: Graduate lecture notes on GCT
milestones.work: K. Mulmuley and M. Sohoni, Geometric Complexity Theory: Introduction, arXiv:0709.0746 (2007)
milestones.description: Public lecture notes systematically introduce the GCT programme.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the lecture notes to 2007.

works.citation: Geometric Complexity Theory I: An Approach to the P vs. NP and Related Problems

notes: The title itself supplies a reproducible naming anchor in 2001. First successful target application and formal institutional recognition remain open.

milestones.label: Higher topoi developed in homotopical algebraic geometry
milestones.work: B. Toën and G. Vezzosi, Homotopical Algebraic Geometry I: Topos theory, arXiv:math/0207028 (2002)
milestones.description: The public preprint investigates higher topoi using simplicially enriched categories and develops higher sites and stacks.

evidence.claim: ArXiv gives the public July 2002 submission and the abstract explicitly describes higher topoi.

milestones.label: Lurie’s higher-topos manuscript
milestones.work: J. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, arXiv:math/0608040 (2006)
milestones.description: The public manuscript develops higher versions of Grothendieck topoi using quasicategories.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the public manuscript to August 2006 and states its purpose.

milestones.label: Higher Topos Theory book published
milestones.work: J. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Princeton University Press (2009)
milestones.description: The Princeton monograph gives systematic treatment of quasicategories and higher topoi.

works.citation: Homotopical Algebraic Geometry I: Topos theory

notes: The 2002 Toën–Vezzosi preprint already investigates higher topoi, four years before Lurie’s public manuscript; the 2005 journal issue is not the conceptual start. The 2009 book is a later consolidation. Related Rezk and Joyal precursors and first target application remain to be adjudicated.

milestones.label: PRIMES is in P posted publicly
milestones.work: M. Agrawal, N. Kayal and N. Saxena, PRIMES is in P, IIT Kanpur public preprint (2002)
milestones.description: The publicly posted paper gives an unconditional deterministic polynomial-time primality algorithm.

evidence.claim: Original paper is dated 6 August 2002; IIT and contemporary accounts confirm public posting.

milestones.label: Annals version published
milestones.work: M. Agrawal, N. Kayal and N. Saxena, PRIMES is in P, Ann. Math. 160 (2004)
milestones.description: The journal version publishes the AKS result in Annals of Mathematics.

notes: The 2002 public posting is the conceptual date, not the date printed in the Annals volume. A separate first application and institutional date remain open.

milestones.label: Cluster algebras introduced publicly
milestones.work: S. Fomin and A. Zelevinsky, Cluster algebras I: Foundations, arXiv:math/0104151 (2001)
milestones.description: The preprint initiates a class of commutative algebras motivated by canonical bases and total positivity.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the public preprint to April 2001 and states the new class.

notes: The 2002 JAMS paper followed the 2001 public preprint. First purposeful use on a target problem and dedicated institutional recognition require further research.

milestones.label: Heegaard Floer invariants introduced
milestones.work: P. Ozsváth and Z. Szabó, Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds, arXiv:math/0101206 (2001)
milestones.description: The public preprint defines three-manifold invariants from Heegaard splittings and holomorphic disks.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the preprint to January 2001 and describes the invariants.

works.citation: Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds

notes: The 2004 Annals version is later than the 2001 public preprint. First application to a distinct target theorem and named institutional anchor remain open.
